nodes.summary: A protocol for the processes `G` with inputs in `V`, local states `σ` and messages `M`. Process `i` starts in state `init i x` from its input `x`; in each round `r` every process `j` sends `send r j s i` to every process `i`, where `s` is its state, and then moves to `recv r i s msg`, where `msg j` is the message it received from `j`; at the end process `i` decides `decide i s`.
nodes.title: Synchronous Byzantine agreement protocol

nodes.summary: After `T` rounds all correct processes decide the same value.
nodes.title: Agreement condition of Byzantine agreement

nodes.summary: The value process `i` decides after `T` rounds.
nodes.title: Decision of a process in Byzantine agreement

nodes.summary: The message of the agreement protocol that a message of `toOral` carries, or `m₀` if it carries none.
nodes.title: Protocol message carried by a later message

nodes.summary: If there are exactly two processes and at least two values, no deterministic synchronous protocol reaches Byzantine agreement with at most $m \ge 1$ faulty processes, in any number of rounds.
nodes.title: No synchronous protocol for two processes reaches Byzantine agreement with one fault

nodes.summary: Let there be at least two values and $n$ processes with $3 \le n \le 3m$. Then no deterministic synchronous protocol reaches Byzantine agreement with at most $m$ faulty processes, in any number of rounds: for every protocol and every number of rounds $T$ there are inputs, a set of at most $m$ faulty processes and a behaviour of the faulty processes for which agreement or validity fails after $T$ rounds.
nodes.title: No synchronous protocol reaches Byzantine agreement when $3 \le n \le 3m$

nodes.summary: Let there be at least two values and $n$ processes with $2 \le n \le 3m$. Then no deterministic synchronous protocol reaches Byzantine agreement with at most $m$ faulty processes, in any number of rounds. With a single process the statement fails: deciding one's own input tolerates one fault.
nodes.title: No synchronous protocol reaches Byzantine agreement when $2 \le n \le 3m$

nodes.summary: Let there be at least two values. No deterministic synchronous protocol for three processes reaches Byzantine agreement with one faulty process, in any number of rounds. This is the case $n = 3$, $m = 1$ of the general bound, which Fischer, Lynch and Merritt (1986, §3.1) prove first, by the hexagon argument: six copies of the three devices, arranged in a ring with inputs $0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1$, look locally like three…
nodes.title: No synchronous protocol for three processes reaches Byzantine agreement with one fault

nodes.summary: The order a message of `toOral` carries, or `d` if it carries none.
nodes.title: Order carried by a first-round message

nodes.summary: If `Q` reaches Byzantine agreement with at most `m` faulty processes in `T` rounds, then `Q.toOral c d m₀` solves the Byzantine generals problem with commander `c` and at most `m` traitors in `T + 1` rounds.
nodes.title: Byzantine agreement yields the Byzantine generals problem

nodes.summary: `Q` reaches Byzantine agreement with at most `m` faulty processes in `T` rounds: agreement and validity hold for all inputs, every set of at most `m` faulty processes and every behaviour of the faulty processes.
nodes.title: Reaching Byzantine agreement

nodes.summary: After round `r + 1` of `Q.toOral c d m₀` with order `v` and traitors `traitors`, every loyal general `i` holds its state after round `r` of `Q` with input the order it received from the commander, the same faulty processes, and faulty messages read off the traitors' messages.
nodes.title: The commander protocol simulates the agreement protocol

nodes.summary: `Q.state x faulty adv r i` is the state of process `i` after `r` rounds of `Q` with inputs `x` and faulty processes `faulty`, where a faulty process `j` sends `adv r j i` to process `i` in round `r`. Correct processes follow the protocol.
nodes.title: Executions of a Byzantine agreement protocol

nodes.summary: In a round `r + 1`, `toOral` runs round `r` of the agreement protocol.
nodes.title: Later rounds of the commander protocol

nodes.summary: In a round `r + 1`, `toOral` sends the message of round `r` of the agreement protocol.
nodes.title: Later messages of the commander protocol

nodes.summary: The oral-message protocol with commander `c` built from `Q`: in round `0` the commander sends its order to every general, and every general takes the order it received from `c` as its input to `Q` (`d` if the message carries no order); in round `r + 1` the generals run round `r` of `Q`. A general decides as in `Q`, or `d` before the first round. The default message `m₀` replaces messages of the wrong kind, which…
nodes.title: Byzantine generals from Byzantine agreement

nodes.summary: If all correct processes have the same input `v`, then after `T` rounds every correct process decides `v`.
nodes.title: Validity condition of Byzantine agreement

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
